packages.label: נָבָל וְהַתּוֹרָה
packages.reason: The only bechina edge in Torah #123 equates נָבָל with תּוֹרָה. The Rebbe establishes the equation in two complementary ways: (1) נָבָל as an acrostic — ל"ב נְתִיבוֹת (the 32 Paths of Wisdom), which is the totality/generality (כְּלָלִיּוּת) of Torah; (2) נָבָל as linguistically related to נוֹבְלוֹת — 'Torah is called noblot chochma ha'elyona' (Bereishit Rabbah 17), meaning Torah is the fallen-off sparks of the supernal wisdom, the accessible face of divine Chochma. Both paths arrive at the same conclusion: naval IS a bechina of Torah — they share the essential nature of true, divine wisdom that supersedes and nullifies all external wisdoms. This is the structural heart of the teaching: the word 'naval' (seemingly 'vile/degraded') in Onkelos's translation of Devarim 32:6 encodes the highest reality — Torah, the true wisdom before which all human wisdoms are null.
merge_notes: Raw connected component: single edge {נבל, תורה} — one component of 2 nodes. No merging required or possible; this is the entire bechina graph for Torah #123.

Although the Torah discusses חָכְמוֹת (wisdoms), כְּפִירָה (heresy), אֱמֶת (truth), תַּם וְיָשָׁר (simplicity), and קַבָּלַת הַתּוֹרָה (receiving the Torah), none of these appear as nodes in bechina edges for reference 123 — they operate exclusively through eitza (cause-and-effect) edges or narrative description. Per framework rules, packages are built on bechina edges only; eitza-only nodes are not assigned to packages.
